summary: Sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan that turns into a live call review of Andrew Musial's call with a prospect named Tom (the 07/03 'Impromptu Zoom Meeting' recording in the same batch). Chris plays back the recording and coaches Andrew that he rebutted rather than listened, that the stated spouse objection was really a money objection, and that he never ran a proper open-wallet before trying to close. The team discusses the deposit process, how to handle a spouse objection ('are they around?'), an automation system that has been spamming prospects with reschedule reminders, and announces a move to daily sales meetings plus two new setters joining.
notable: Deposit policy stated as company process: a fully refundable $100 or $500 deposit is taken to secure a second conversation, and the scripted justification is 'we do a deposit with people because we don't do any follow-ups, don't put people back on the calendar because we get so busy' — contradicted in the same call by Chris coaching a follow-up message and reps saying they will 'hit some follow-up'.

Richard Claessen recommends calling non-responsive prospects from an unrecognised number so they answer: 'if you call someone on the number that they know you from, they're not responding. But if you then call them with a random number, they pick up.'
Automated outreach ('Sophia' / the booking bot) is spamming prospects with reschedule and start-time messages; a prospect previously called it out on a live call as obviously automated.

Extended homophobic banter about a paying prospect ('hat-trick', 'three gay guys in a row', 'Mr. Gay Guy', 'you just have to go on a date with him'). Chris Klevan pushed back once — 'Tom is just a guy. It doesn't matter who he's attracted to' — and Richard Claessen noted 'you're saying it because there's recorders in here.'
Chris confirms Andrew never ran an open wallet on Tom: 'Did you open wallet him, Andrew?' / 'Nope, not properly.'
Process change announced: daily sales team meetings Monday to Friday, plus a new setter and a DM setter joining.
Richard Claessen states a Dutch prospect could never have been closed because Dutch healthcare would not reimburse — a market-fit observation about inbound lead quality.
